title: Introduction and Snake Rag with King Oliver
summary: Gleason introduces Armstrong and plays Snake Rag from the 1923 King Oliver Creole Jazz Band record.

blocks.x: Song Song This is Jazz Casual, I'm Ralph Gleason, and that voice and that music is the voice and

music of jazz as number one ambassador to the world, Louis Armstrong, who is with us today to talk about some of his music. Louis, welcome to Jazz Casual. Thank you very much. It's an honor to have you here, and I'm sure that, like many other people that have been interested in jazz, have been fans of jazz, I can say that I grew up loving this music, and this means that I grew up loving you, and been fascinated by it, and fascinated by the things you've done, and I've wanted to know so many different things about the records that you've made. You've been recording now for, oh, 40 years, the first record you made back with King Oliver in Chicago in 1923. I thought it might be interesting if we could play for our audience some of these records and then talk to you about them a little bit, and if we could start out hearing the King Oliver Creole Jazz Band with Louis Armstrong and King Oliver on cornets playing Snake Rag.
